sigmoids are associated with geoeffective MCs that show a distinct solar-terrestrial correlation.

the magnetic field of a MC associated with a coronal eruption is not predictable.
the magnetic fields of MCs associated to sigmoids are more complex than those associated to filament eruptions.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the properties of the magnetic clouds associated with sigmoidal eruptions are not predictable from the observed coronal magnetic field structure.
, although there are some similarities between the magnetic fields of erupting sigmolds and those of erupting filaments, there are significant differences as well.
sigmoids and filaments are two distinct types of solar magnetic structures, and that their associated magnetic clouds are two distinct classes of events.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, while sigmoids are an important source of magnetic clouds and storms, they are not well understood.
the solar-terrestrial relationship of MCs depends strongly on the structure of the source region of the eruption.
, while sigmoids and filaments are both manifestations of a magnetic null in the corona, they are not necessarily associated with the same magnetic topology.
